screens.title: Welcome
screens.text: This app prepares you for the COS212 lecture on AVL trees. It has nine short lessons that take about an hour in total. You will see why a binary search tree can become slow, how an AVL tree keeps itself balanced, and how search, rotations and insertion work.

screens.title: Your route
screens.text: The app has nine lessons, listed below. You can stop after any lesson and continue later from where you left off. By the end of the lessons, you will be able to do the following.
points: C1 Getting started and readiness check
C2 When BSTs go lopsided
C3 The AVL property
C4 Search (the algorithm)
C5 Rotations
C6 Insertion with rebalancing
C7 Deletion with rebalancing (optional)
C8 Choosing a structure
C9 Am I ready for the lecture?
objectives: Explain how AVL trees fix the problem of lopsided BSTs (LO1).
Calculate heights and balance factors, and decide whether a tree is an AVL tree (LO2).
Trace a search in an AVL tree, and explain why it takes O(log n) steps (LO3).
Choose and perform the rotation or rotations that restore the balance (LO4).
Insert keys into an AVL tree and rebalance it (LO5).
Judge when an AVL tree is a good choice, and explain why (LO6).
Delete a leaf and restore the AVL property (LO7, optional).

screens.title: How the app works
points: The Next and Back buttons are always in the same place. The Replay button shows the current step again.
The Show the rule button opens a short summary of the key rule on the current screen.
The Hint button tells you what a question checks and which idea it relies on.
When you answer a question, tap Sure or Not sure to show how confident you are. This helps the app find ideas that need another look.
You can try a practice task as many times as you like. You can re-attempt each check question once.
After each check, you receive a title from Structural Savant to Complexity Cadet, together with a suggested next step.
You can open any lesson that you have completed from the lesson list.

screens.title: The conventions card
screens.text: These conventions follow the COS212 slides. You can open this card from the menu at any time.
points: The height of a node is the number of edges on the longest path from that node down to a leaf. A leaf has height 0, and an empty branch has height −1.

The balance factor (bf) of a node is the height of its right branch minus the height of its left branch, bf = h(right) − h(left). The valid values are −1, 0 and +1, and a negative value means that the left branch is taller.
The unbalanced node is called n, and its children are n.left and n.right.
The names Case 1 (LL), Case 2 (LR), Case 3 (RL) and Case 4 (RR) describe where a new key went below n.
O(lg n) and O(log n) mean the same thing.
screens.caption: Node 20 has a balance factor of 1 − 0 = +1. Node 40 has a balance factor of 0 − 0 = 0. Each leaf has a balance factor of −1 − (−1) = 0.

screens.title: The BST rule
screens.text: In a binary search tree, every key in a node's left subtree is smaller than the node, and every key in its right subtree is larger. Every subtree is itself a BST.
screens.caption: 5 is the root. 3 and 1 are smaller, so they are on the left. 7, 6 and 9 are larger, so they are on the right.

screens.title: Searching a BST
screens.text: Start at the root and compare the key with the node. If they are equal, stop. If the key is smaller, go left. If it is larger, go right.
steps: 6 is larger than 5, so the search goes right.
6 is smaller than 7, so the search goes left.
6 equals 6, so the key is found.

screens.title: Inserting into a BST
screens.text: Search for the new key. It goes into the empty branch where the search ends, so it always becomes a leaf.
steps: 4 is smaller than 5, so the search goes left.
4 is larger than 3, so the search goes right.
4 goes into the empty right branch of 3.
Node 3 now has a balance factor of 0 − 0 = 0.
Node 5 now has a balance factor of 1 − 1 = 0.
Every node now has a balance factor of −1, 0 or +1.

screens.title: Tree terms and height
points: The root has no parent. A leaf has no children. Nodes with the same parent are siblings.
The height of a node is the number of edges on the longest path from that node down to a leaf.
Here the leaves 1, 6 and 9 have height 0, nodes 3 and 7 have height 1, and the root, 5, has height 2.

task.stem: 8 is about to be inserted. Click the node that will become the parent of 8.
task.hint: This question checks BST insertion. Search for the new key, and it goes into the empty branch where the search ends.

wrongAnswers.feedback: 7 already has a right child, 9, so the search continues. 8 is smaller than 9, so 8 goes into the empty left branch of 9.

feedback.correct: 8 is larger than 5, so the search goes right. 8 is larger than 7, so it goes right again. 8 is smaller than 9, so it goes left. The left branch of 9 is empty, so 8 becomes the left child of 9.
feedback.incorrect: 8 is larger than 5, so the search goes right. 8 is larger than 7, so it goes right again. 8 is smaller than 9, so it goes left. The left branch of 9 is empty, so 8 becomes the left child of 9.
